{{Quote|There's something alive in here.|Luke Skywalker|<ref name="Episode 4">{{Film|IV}}</ref>}}
'''Dianoga''' were large [[Cephalopod/Legends|cephalopods]], capable of growing up to ten [[Meter/Legends|meters]] in length, though most specimens grew to approximately five or six meters. They had a single [[Ommatophora|eyestalk]] protruding from their mollusk-like bodies, and seven suckered tentacles surrounding a fanged maw containing a sharp serrated probe. Their life cycle begun with an egg.<ref>{{TORcite|exp=lots|type=other|A crate with "Dianoga eggs" seen at the [[Sporefall]] forward camp on [[Dantooine/Legends|Dantooine]]}}</ref>

==History==
[[File:Dianoga-woswfg.jpg|thumb|left|180px|A dianoga's fanged maw]]
{{Quote|I've seen these things before. Last time I ran into one was in a trash compactor. It nearly got me.|Luke Skywalker|<ref name="SOTE">[[Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire (novel)|''Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire'' novel]]</ref>}}
The muddy-colored [[Squid/Legends|squid]]-like<ref name=":0" /> dianoga originated on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Vodran/Legends|Vodran]],<ref name="BtM" /> discovered by the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutts]] prior to the formation of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], where the creatures evolved a form of natural camouflage to disguise themselves and avoid the planet's large predators. They learned to change color<ref name=":2">''[[Galaxy Guide 12: Aliens — Enemies and Allies]]''</ref> and scavenge.<ref name="The Movie Trilogy Sourcebook">''[[The Movie Trilogy Sourcebook]]''</ref> Their bodies would become transparent when unfed, and, conversely, were known to change to reflect the color of the food they had eaten. This was achieved by diverting small portions of digested food into a series of ducts underneath the creature's skin, which would appear to affect the color of the dianoga's flesh.<ref name=":1" />

Over many millennia, dianoga migrated from Vodran by stowing away aboard garbage ships in their microscopic larval forms,<ref name=":2" /> and could be commonly found in trash compactors, garbage pits, and sewers across [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]], living off any present organic matter. They were primarily scavengers, and only posed a threat to living creatures when starving or threatened. Because of their penchant for living in and feeding on organic waste, dianoga were sometimes referred to as '''garbage squids''',<ref name=":1">''[[Galaxy Guide 1: A New Hope]]''</ref> '''sewage squids''', or '''trash monsters'''. Before being officially documented and known to the [[galactic community]], it was mainly maintainance workers who witnessed the legendary "sewer creatures", and their reports were often met with scepticism.<ref name="Dark Forces Manual: Coded Transmissions">''[[Dark Forces Manual: Coded Transmissions]]''</ref>

[[File:Dianoga_in_Toilets.jpg|left|thumb|A dianoga exiting from a toilet in a [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] apartment.]]
Dianoga would often prove a nuisance by nesting in bodies of water, sewage systems, and whatever other large concentrations of dirty, appalling liquid that they could locate. Smaller dianoga were even known to crawl out of [[Toilet/Legends|toilets]].<ref name="WSWFG" /> Despite this, they could prove useful, since they served to rid waste of biological material, leaving behind salvageable minerals and metals. Only when a dianoga grew too large was it usually considered a threat, especially in urban areas such as [[Galactic City/Legends|Galactic City]] on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]. Indeed, in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], Coruscant's [[Desrini District]] experienced a dianoga infestation, following an incident with a misfiring garbage launcher. Up to twenty-five residents were reported to have been attacked by the scavengers, and it was believed the creatures would quickly spread to neighboring districts.<ref name="Hnn-Desrini Plagued by Dianogas">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|55|news/1359_3.html|Desrini Plagued by Dianogas}}</ref> The presence of a single dianoga was often cause for alarm, since the creatures were self-fertilizing hermaphrodites,<ref name="WSWFG" /> and could quickly multiply to pose a larger problem.

[[File:DianogaEye-ANH.png|180px|thumb|A dianoga's central eye.]]

[[Unidentified Dianoga|One dianoga]] was known to have boarded the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|first Death Star]], and made its home in one of the [[Space station/Legends|space station's]] [[Garbage Compactor 3263827|garbage compactors]]. When [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]], [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]], and [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]], during the rescue of Leia, were forced into the trash compactor, the dianoga attacked Skywalker. It pulled the young farmboy under the murky, polluted water, but was scared away when the compactor walls activated.<ref name="Episode 4" /> The dianoga itself had managed to burrow into the wall, and so was relatively safe inside the compactor; that is, until the Death Star was destroyed.<ref name="Episode 4" />

Another infestation of dianoga was experienced by [[Dash Rendar/Legends|Dash Rendar]] in the sewers beneath Prince [[Xizor/Legends|Xizor's]] palace. Upon exiting the sewers, Dash was forced to fight a [[Giant dianoga|full grown dianoga]], which was at least 10 meters long.<ref name="Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire video game">[[Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire (video game)|''Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire'' video game]]</ref>

Dianoga were also found on [[Anoat/Legends|Anoat]], where several attacked [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] mercenary [[Kyle Katarn]] as he worked through the sewers in an effort to locate [[Moff/Legends|Moff]] [[Rebus (Galactic Empire)|Rebus]], in his campaign against the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[Dark Trooper Project]].<ref name="DF">''[[Star Wars: Dark Forces]]''</ref>

Dianoga could be found in the sewers of Coruscant and many other locations across the galaxy.<ref name="WSWFG" /> Their flesh was used in the making of [[dianoga pie]],<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Alien Species">''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]''</ref> and their spleens could be processed to make [[Dianogan tea/Legends|Dianogan tea]], a beverage notably favored by [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Pors Tonith/Legends|Pors Tonith]]. [[Dianoga cream]] was used in [[Dianoga cream-filled donut]]s which were served in [[Dex's Diner/Legends|Dex's Diner]].<ref name="Dining at Dex's">{{Hyperspace|url=fans/hyperspace/source/dexdiner/index.html|text=Dining at Dex's|int=Dining at Dex's}}</ref>

At least a [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Unidentified dianoga-like species|species]], which included the [[Vodran/Legends|Vodran]]-native [[Niado Duegad]],<ref name="Card-CCG-Niado Duegad">{{CCG|set=Special Edition Limited|cardname=Niado Duegad}}</ref> was notably similar to dianoga.<ref name="The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia">{{CSWECite|I|213|Duegad, Niado}}</ref>

The [[Dargul Dianogas]]''',''' a [[Shockball/Legends|shockball]] team from the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Dargul]], were named after dianoga.<ref name="Secrets of the Sisar Run">''[[Secrets of the Sisar Run]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
The name "dianoga", one of the oldest terms in [[Star Wars|''Star Wars'' lore]], originated in the [[The Star Wars first draft|first draft]] of the script for ''[[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|A New Hope]]'', where the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] were called Dai Nogas, or occasionally just "Dai." This evolved into Jedi, and dianoga (or variations thereof) came to describe a nasty creature lurking about in the garbage, as the early scripts didn't always have the [[Garbage Compactor 3263827|trash compactor]] aboard the [[Death Star/Legends|Death Star]].<ref name=":0" /> The Revised Fourth Draft of [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']] mentions this creature as Dia Nogu.

The original [[Kenner Products|Kenner]] toy for the Death Star playset, designed by [[Tim Effler]], included a Dianoga in its trash compactor. The soft rubber form resembled a green, mutant shark with an eye stalk protruding from its nose and its fins ending with tentacles.<ref>{{KennerCite|set=Star Wars (Kenner toy line)|pack=Death Star Space Station|link=Kenner-PS-DeathStar1.asp}}</ref>

In the final film, director [[George Lucas]] was reportedly less than impressed with the delivered dianoga effect, having envisioned something bigger and more ominous.<ref name=":0">{{DB|creature|dianoga|dianoga}}</ref>
